items.heading: Cleaning a gas stove burner with a clogged or uneven flame
precautionsFirst: Turn off the gas supply at the cylinder or valve before cleaning.
Make sure burner parts are completely dry before reassembling and lighting, to avoid an irregular flame.
details: Turn off the gas and let the burner cool completely.
Remove the burner cap and ring, and soak them in warm water with dish soap or a little vinegar for 15-20 minutes.
Scrub the burner holes with an old toothbrush or a fine wire or needle to clear clogged ports.
Rinse and dry thoroughly, then wipe the stovetop and igniter area with a damp cloth.
Reassemble the burner parts in the correct order and test ignition.

items.heading: Gas stove clicking but not lighting
precautionsFirst: If you smell gas, do not attempt ignition - turn off the supply, ventilate the area, and call a technician.
details: Check the burner cap and ring are seated correctly and aligned.
Clean the igniter tip and burner ports of food debris or moisture.
Check the gas supply valve is fully open and the cylinder is not empty.
If it still does not ignite, the igniter or battery in electronic-ignition stoves may need replacing - a simple swap most people can do with the manual.

items.heading: Washing machine not draining water
precautionsFirst: Switch off and unplug the machine before checking the drain filter or hose.
Keep a shallow tray ready, as some residual water will spill out.
details: Check the drain hose is not kinked, blocked, or positioned too high.
Open the drain filter or pump filter, usually a small door at the front-bottom, and clean out lint, coins, or debris.
Check for an error code on the display and refer to the manual for what it means.
If draining still fails after cleaning, the drain pump itself may be faulty - this typically needs a technician.

items.heading: Washing machine not spinning
precautionsFirst: Do not overload the machine beyond its rated capacity, which is a common cause of spin failure.
details: Check the load is balanced - redistribute clothes evenly if it is lopsided.
Make sure the lid or door is closing and latching fully, since most machines will not spin with an open door detected.
Check the machine is level on the floor, as unlevel machines can trigger safety cutoffs.
If the issue persists, the belt or motor may need a technician's attention.

items.heading: Washing machine making a loud noise during a cycle
precautionsFirst: Stop the cycle and unplug the machine before inspecting the drum.
details: Check for coins, buttons, or small objects trapped between the drum and the outer tub.
Make sure the machine is on a level, stable surface, adding rubber pads under the feet if needed.
Check the load is not unbalanced, such as heavy items bunched on one side.
If noise continues with an empty, balanced load, the bearings or motor mount may need professional inspection.

items.heading: Refrigerator not cooling properly
precautionsFirst: Do not overload the fridge or block the internal vents with food items.
details: Check the temperature dial or setting has not been accidentally changed.
Clean the condenser coils at the back or bottom of the fridge, which can accumulate dust and reduce efficiency.
Check the door seal by closing it on a piece of paper and gently pulling - if it slides out easily, the seal needs replacing.
Ensure a few inches of clearance behind and around the fridge for ventilation.
If cooling issues persist, the compressor or refrigerant gas may need professional servicing.

items.heading: Refrigerator making an unusual noise
precautionsFirst: Unplug the fridge before inspecting its stability.
details: Check the fridge is level, adjusting the leveling feet at the base if it rocks.
Make sure nothing is touching the back or sides that could vibrate against it.
Clear the top of the fridge of items that could rattle.
A persistent grinding or clicking noise may indicate a compressor or fan issue needing a technician.

items.heading: Microwave not heating food
precautionsFirst: Never operate a microwave with an open, damaged, or improperly sealed door.
Do not attempt to open the microwave's outer casing yourself - it can retain a dangerous electrical charge even when unplugged.
details: Check the door is closing fully and latching, since microwaves have safety switches that block heating if the door is not sealed.
Test with a cup of water for a minute - if it does not warm at all, the magnetron may have failed.
Check the power supply, plug, and any household fuse or breaker for that socket.
If the fault is confirmed internal, call a qualified technician rather than opening the unit yourself.

items.heading: Mixer grinder motor humming but blade not turning
precautionsFirst: Always unplug before opening or cleaning the jar assembly or blades.
Do not overload the jar beyond the recommended capacity, especially with hard items.
details: Check the jar is seated and locked correctly on the base, since most mixers have a safety interlock.
Check for food debris jammed around the blade coupling at the base of the jar.
Let the motor cool for 15-20 minutes if it has been overused and tripped a thermal cutoff.
Check the power cord and socket for a proper connection.
If the motor hums but the blade does not turn, the carbon brushes or coupling may be worn and need a technician's replacement.

items.heading: Water purifier (RO) not working or low output
precautionsFirst: Turn off and unplug the unit before checking the filters.
details: Check the inlet water supply valve is open and there is adequate pressure.
Check the pre-filter, or sediment filter, for clogging - a heavily discolored filter needs replacing.
Check the storage tank valve is open, if the unit has a tank.
Filters typically need replacing every 6-12 months depending on usage - check the manual for the schedule.
If the pump does not run at all, this likely needs a technician.

items.heading: Ceiling fan wobbling
precautionsFirst: Switch off the fan and let the blades come to a complete stop before touching them.
details: Clean each blade and check they are all equally free of dust buildup, which can unbalance the fan.
Check all blades are at the same height by measuring from each blade tip to the ceiling.
Tighten any loose screws at the blade brackets and the mounting point.
Use a fan-balancing clip kit, inexpensive and available online, if wobbling continues after these checks.

items.heading: Ceiling fan running slow even at top speed
precautionsFirst: Turn off power at the switch before inspecting the regulator area, and leave capacitor replacement to an electrician due to shock risk.
details: Check the speed regulator is not itself faulty by testing another fan on the same switch if possible.
Clean dust from the fan motor housing, which can cause overheating and reduced speed.
A weak or faulty capacitor is a common cause of slow speed - this small, inexpensive part should be replaced by an electrician.

items.heading: Geyser or water heater not heating
precautionsFirst: Never open the geyser's internal panel without switching off both power and the water supply - there is a risk of electric shock and scalding.
Let the unit cool if it was recently used before checking anything.
details: Check the power switch and indicator light are on, and the thermostat is set to an adequate temperature.
Check the household breaker for that circuit has not tripped.
Reset the safety thermal cutout button, if the geyser has one, following the manual.
If there is no power fault and it still does not heat, the heating element likely needs replacement - call a technician, as this involves electrical work.

items.heading: Vacuum cleaner losing suction
precautionsFirst: Unplug before opening the dust compartment or checking the hoses.
details: Empty the dust bag or canister if it is more than two-thirds full.
Check and clean or replace the filters, which clog with fine dust over time.
Check the hose and brush roller for tangled hair, thread, or blockages, and clear them out.
Make sure the roller brush spins freely and is not jammed.

items.heading: Iron not heating or not producing steam
precautionsFirst: Always unplug the iron before checking the water tank or soleplate, and let it cool if recently used.
details: Check the temperature dial is set correctly for the fabric, and the power cord and socket are working.
For steam issues, check the water tank has enough water and is filled correctly.
If steam vents look clogged with mineral deposits, run a vinegar-water mix through the steam function, then flush with plain water.
If it still does not heat with a confirmed working socket, the internal heating element likely needs professional repair.

items.heading: Air conditioner not cooling well
precautionsFirst: Switch off the AC and its breaker before cleaning the filter.
Do not attempt to open the outdoor unit or handle refrigerant lines yourself.
details: Clean or wash the air filter, the most common cause of reduced cooling, and let it dry fully before reinserting.
Check the temperature and mode settings on the remote.
Make sure the outdoor unit has clear airflow, free of dust, leaves, or obstructions.
Check doors and windows in the room are closed properly.
If cooling is still poor, the refrigerant level or compressor may need a professional technician's check.
